---
title: A page in the Tufte theme
subtitle: Type, measure and rules after Tufte CSS
---

This page shows the theme. The text is set in ET Book, on a paper that is
not quite white. The lines are short, so the eye finds the next one. A
[link](https://edwardtufte.github.io/tufte-css/) is the colour of the text,
with a thin rule under it.

## Headings

A second-level heading is in italic, as in Tufte's books. So is a heading of
the third level.

### A smaller heading

Each heading has the normal weight. There is no rule under it.

## Code

Code is set in Consolas, a little smaller than the text, as in `print(x)`.

```python
def mean(xs: list[float]) -> float:
    "The mean of the numbers."
    return sum(xs) / len(xs)
```

## Callouts

::: {.callout-note}
A note has a thin rule at its left, in a muted blue.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## A warning with a title
The title is in italic.
:::

## A table

A table has a heavy rule above and below, and a light one under the header.

| Book                               | Year | Pages |
|:-----------------------------------|-----:|------:|
| The Visual Display of Quantitative Information | 1983 | 197 |
| Envisioning Information            | 1990 | 126 |
| Visual Explanations                | 1997 | 156 |
| Beautiful Evidence                 | 2006 | 213 |

> The commonality between science and art is in trying to see profoundly.
